No, they're not forcing people to pay for upgrades. They're turning off 3G. And that's not happening until March of 2022, meaning they're providing almost two years of notice before that happens.

To give you an idea of how old a phone would have to be in order to be affected by this, AT&T's site lists the phones that will still work. One of the tables says "iPhone 6 or newer."

The iPhone 6 was released five years ago. The previous generation seven years ago. Meaning by the time they turn off 3G, affected devices will be at least nine years old.

Sure, it sucks to not be able to use a perfectly working device, but let's not pretend this is some sudden thing. The number of ancient devices affected by this will be quite small, which is the same reason they're turning off 3G to begin with; not enough people using it to make it worthwhile.

But since it's a material change in the offering, holdouts could potentially use this to negotiate a good deal on a newer device. OR, since these holdouts obviously don't care about all the new features, they don't need an overpriced flagship on a payment plan. They can just pickup a slightly newer, completely unlocked device for cheap. And if they get an unlocked device, they can easily take it with them should they decide to switch carriers for whatever reason.

tl;dr - This isn't the sinister conspiracy people make it out to be. Any 3G-only phones that still work are going to be in the vanishing minority, and those people can get by with a cheap, slightly newer toy.
